title: Internal modules with profinite condensed-group actions and normalized invariants
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the coherent profinite site, in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\mathcal M_R$ for its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and use the section modules and restriction maps of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For a topological group $P$, define $\mathcal A_P(R)$ to have an internal module $M$ together with homomorphisms $C(S,P)\to\operatorname{End}_{R(S)}(M(S))$ natural in all profinite $S$. Morphisms are internal linear maps commuting with these actions on every section module. Equivariant maps contain identities and zero and are closed under composition, sums and negatives; give this category its resulting sectionwise additive structure and forgetful functor to $\mathcal M_R$. For a continuous homomorphism $\pi:P\to Q$, inflation precomposes the action by $C(S,\pi)$ and leaves underlying modules and maps unchanged. Trivial inflation from $\mathcal M_R$ gives the identity action.

A section $m\in M(S)$ is kernel-fixed if, for every $f:T\to S$ and $g\in C(T,P)$ with $\pi\circ g=1$, one has $g\cdot f^*m=f^*m$. It is fully fixed if the same condition holds for every $g\in C(T,P)$ without a kernel restriction. A normalized invariants datum consists of an additive functor to $\mathcal M_R$, an inclusion into the underlying-module functor which is injective on sections with image exactly the fully fixed sections, and an adjunction from trivial inflation whose forward transpose restricts the codomain along this inclusion and whose inverse composes with the inclusion. For $P=G\times H$ and $\pi=\operatorname{pr}_G$, a normalized product invariants datum instead has an additive functor to $\mathcal A_G(R)$, an underlying-module inclusion with image exactly the kernel-fixed sections, an adjunction from projection inflation with the same transpose formulas, and the residual $G$-action induced by $(g,1)$. These are specifications of the data; existence is the assertion of the consuming theorem.
